\[
E = \sigma\Big(\sum_{k} a_k\, s_k(x) + b\Big)
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(s_k\): The side output at one scale
- \(a_k, b\): The learned fusion weights
- \(E\): The edge probability

Both networks make several side outputs s_k, edge maps at different scales, upsampled to the image size. A learned weighting a_k fuses them, and a sigmoid gives the edge probability. HED takes its side outputs from the five stages of VGG16. PiDiNet builds its convolutions from differences between neighbors, so they act like learned gradient operators.
